correctness.rationale: Every subgroup outside A meets A in a subgroup B containing <y> and has exactly one outside coset xγB, so the parametrization H(B,x) is exhaustive and unique modulo B. Direct multiplication shows H(B,x) and H(C,z) permute exactly when (xz^{-1})^2 lies in BC. The difference map A/B x A/C -> A/BC is surjective with fiber size |A:B∩C|, so the number of acceptable coset pairs is exactly |A:B∩C| times the size of the 2-torsion of A/BC. This yields the subgroup formula after accounting for the normal subgroups contained in A. The cyclic formula is the B=C=<y> specialization. Brute-force subgroup enumeration agrees on all packaged examples and reproduces the published ordinary-dicyclic and C2-by-cyclic numerical cases.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly identifies arbitrary abelian kernels as the remaining generalized-dicyclic case. The new theorem gives a uniform exact subgroup classification, a sharp pairwise permutability criterion, and formulas for both subgroup and cyclic-subgroup commutativity degrees. It simultaneously explains the ordinary dicyclic and C2 x Cn formulas and isolates a natural quotient 2-torsion term responsible for quaternionic behavior. This is a structural resolution of a named finite-group probability problem rather than a routine special-case computation.
